title: Heap splinter and ghost-cache eviction surge causing cross‑env GPU OOMs
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Summary: Several customers (hosted / dedicated / private) surfaced a correlated uptick in GPU OOMs over the last 10 days. Root cause analysis indicates a converging failure mode: stale tombstone/ghost entries in the KV cache trigger eviction storms which, combined with the allocator's small-chunk splitting behavior, produced heap 'splintering' and high external fragmentation on long-lived inference sessions. The fragmentation prevented large contiguous allocations for KV state and kernel workspace, forcing the runtime to exhaust GPU memory during peak bursts.

Impact: Intermittent but severe across environments: hosted tenants saw degraded tail-latency and 5–12% request failures; Dedicated customers experienced sustained OOM cascades on pinned pools during ML batch windows; Private deployments reported similar memory pressure after long-running canaries. Customer impact: high.

What we've done so far (emergency mitigations):
- Rolled out a short-term fallback to conservative allocator mode for affected runtime pools (hosted canaries -> full rollout for pinned dedicated pools).
- Temporarily disabled prefix-level KV prefetching for high-throughput customers to reduce eviction pressure.
- Added a soft-throttle on concurrent session restores to smooth peak allocation requests.
- Applied a targeted runtime patch (PR #1742) that changes tombstone handling to be transactionally consistent during concurrent evict/insert races.

Technical root cause (investigation notes):
- The KV cache eviction path allowed a narrow race where a key could be marked tombstoned but its slab pointer remained visible to session iterators; iterators then attempted lazy reclamation that produced many sub-sized free blocks.
- The GPU allocator favors splitting for small frees; repeated splits without coalescing produced many narrow free regions (heap splinters). Over time the allocator failed to find large contiguous blocks for model KV, leading to OOMs during cache restores and batched generation.
- Workloads with long-lived KV footprints + high-change rates (chat sessions with frequent tool-calls) were the worst affected.

Planned fix and rollout plan: 
1) Runtime patch set (runtime-1.19):
   - Fix A: Safer tombstone commit ordering and explicit iterator invalidation (PR #1742, merged to feature branch).
   - Fix B: Add background slab coalescer that merges adjacent free extents during low-util windows (PR #1748).
   - Fix C: Add an allocator fallback path that will pre-allocate emergency contiguous chunks for KV restores to avoid OOMs.
2) Canary strategy: Canary in hosted (2% traffic) -> Dedicated pinned pool canaries -> Private customers with opt-in upgrade (staged).
3) Observability: Add new telemetry counters (ghost_tombstone_hits, slab_splinter_ratio, contiguous_block_failures) + dashboards and automated alerts.
4) Tests: Add deterministic reproducer tests in runtime integration suite + fuzz tests for concurrent evict/iterate patterns.

Open trade-offs:
- Background coalescing reduces fragmentation but increases short-term CPU/GPU-side housekeeping. We'll gate coalescer by an adaptive policy that runs during low-percentiles of GPU utilization.
- Pre-allocating emergency chunks reduces OOMs at the cost of slightly lower memory efficiency for some pools; this is optional per pool and configurable by Dedicated customers.

- Incident timeline and logs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/x/frag-incident-2026
- Reproducer (stress harness): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/main/tools/kv-frag-repro
- Runtime PR (tombstone fix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1742
- Runtime PR (coalescer + telemetry): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1748
- Hosted metrics dashboard (internal): https://dashboard.redwood.ai/d/kv-frag/overview

Next steps (owner: Priya Patel):
- Complete unit + integration tests for PR #1748 (ETA: 2026-03-15).
- Run hosted 2% canary for runtime-1.19, monitor slab_splinter_ratio and OOMs for 48h (ETA start: 2026-03-16).
- Coordinate Dedicated canary scheduling with sales/SEs and opt-in Private deploys (ETA: 2026-03-20).
- Post-mortem write-up and customer communication draft (ETA: 2026-03-18).
